Cautiously positive policy stance. The FOMC reaffirms average-inflation targeting and keeps rates at the zero lower bound while extending QE and forward guidance—an approach consistent with the New Keynesian policy-rule literature (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and inflation-forecast targeting frameworks (Svensson and Woodford, 2005). By committing to allow inflation to run moderately above 2%, the Fed aims to anchor expectations near target and reduce real rates, supporting employment. Continued purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS are designed to compress term premia and support credit conditions, in line with QE transmission and term-structure evidence on risk premia (e.g., Cochrane–Piazzesi). However, the statement’s emphasis on COVID-19-related risks and sectoral weakness reflects elevated policy uncertainty, tempering the outlook. Overall tone: mildly optimistic.
